commits.body: The Roadmap tab gains an edit mode, off by default, that requires the local server and says so when it is missing. The run detail drawer stays a read-only reference surface at its own width; editing happens in a centred modal opened from the drawer header. The modal covers every operation the endpoint supports: run title, summary and description, dependencies through a search field rather than a list of every earlier run, status, position, insert, remove and swap, plus phase and objective text. Identity is never editable. Every write is a dry-run first: the preview shows the field diff and the queue_order remap so the cascade is visible before anything is written, and only an explicit confirm sends the apply with the baseline from that preview. Refusals show the core's reason verbatim; a move that would invert a dependency also gets an actionable message naming the offending dependency and the two ways out. A stale baseline, a validator rollback and an unreachable server each get their own honest state. After an apply the roadmap is re-read from disk and re-rendered. All editing code lives in new functions so the validator's pinned source-text assertions keep holding, and additive anchors now pin the edit surface and the two-step flow. Everything outside the Roadmap tab stays read-only.

commits.subject: feat(project-console): add a bounded roadmap write endpoint
commits.body: The console server gains a single POST endpoint that edits roadmap content and nothing else. It imports the roadmap core through a new shared orchestration module that the command line tool now imports too, so both surfaces run the same pipeline and neither reimplements the safety logic. The endpoint fixes the roadmap path, refuses non-local and cross-origin callers, caps the body, serialises writes behind a lock, and uses an optimistic baseline so an apply against a stale read is rejected rather than overwriting. Dry-run returns the queue_order remap; apply writes atomically and the validator remains the authority with rollback. Additive validator anchors pin the route, the handler and the shared import. Objective O0 and the console foundation run said the console mutates nothing; that is now false for roadmap content, so their text states the narrower contract. The console still has no editing UI: that is the next run.

The objective and foundation text that assert a fully read-only console will be corrected when the run executes, since they are still true today.

commits.subject: feat(roadmap): add a command-line tool for safe roadmap edits
commits.body: Hand-editing roadmap.json was the main cost of maintaining the roadmap: every insertion resequences the tail, every move risks inverting a dependency, and a single off-by-one fails the validator. The tool inserts, moves, removes, swaps and edits runs, and edits objective and phase text, resequencing queue_order automatically and refusing any edit that would invert a dependency, create a cycle, orphan a dependency or mutate an identity. Dry-run is the default. Writes are atomic with a backup outside the repo, and the Project Console validator is spawned as the authority after a canonical write, with rollback on failure. The serializer round-trips the file byte-exactly, preserving CRLF and the em-dashes. Core and CLI are split so a future editable console can reuse the core. The console itself stays read-only.
